title: Rigveda 5.85: To Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.85: To Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.85 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 398v-399v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.85.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 30); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 398v
translation.original_text:
1pra sa̱mrāje̍ bṛ̱had a̍rcā gabhī̱ram brahma̍ pri̱yaṁ varu̍ṇāya śru̱tāya̍ | vi yo ja̱ghāna̍ śami̱teva̱ carmo̍pa̱stire̍ pṛthi̱vīṁ sūryā̍ya ||
2vane̍ṣu̱ vy a1̱̍ntari̍kṣaṁ tatāna̱ vāja̱m arva̍tsu̱ paya̍ u̱sriyā̍su | hṛ̱tsu kratu̱ṁ varu̍ṇo a̱psv a1̱̍gniṁ di̱vi sūrya̍m adadhā̱t soma̱m adrau̍ ||
translation.text:
1SING forth a hymn sublime and solemn, grateful to glorious. Varuṇa, imperial Ruler, Who hath struck out, like one who slays the victim, earth as a skin to spread in front of Sûrya.
2In the tree-tops the air he hath extended, put milk in kine and vigorous speed in horses, Set intellect in hearts, fire in the waters, Sûrya in heaven and Soma on the mountain.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 398v (numbered 71v by the scribe) (OPenn image 399, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.84.2 ‹heṣantam perum asyasi arjuni›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 399r (numbered 72r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.85.3 ‹rājā yavam na vṛṣṭiḥ›. Verses 5.85.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pra | sam-rāje | bṛhat | arca | gabhīram | brahma | priyam | varuṇāya | śrutāya | vi | yaḥ | jaghāna | śamitāiva | carma | upa-stire | pṛthivīm | sūryāya
2vaneṣu | vi | antarikṣam | tatāna | vājam | arvat-su | payaḥ | usriyāsu | hṛt-su | kratum | varuṇaḥ | ap-su | agnim | divi | sūryam | adadhāt | somam | adrau

translation.original_ref: RV 5.85.3-6 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 30); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 399r
translation.original_text:
3nī̱cīna̍bāra̱ṁ varu̍ṇa̱ḥ kava̍ndha̱m pra sa̍sarja̱ roda̍sī a̱ntari̍kṣam | tena̱ viśva̍sya̱ bhuva̍nasya̱ rājā̱ yava̱ṁ na vṛ̱ṣṭir vy u̍natti̱ bhūma̍ ||
4u̱natti̱ bhūmi̍m pṛthi̱vīm u̱ta dyāṁ ya̱dā du̱gdhaṁ varu̍ṇo̱ vaṣṭy ād it | sam a̱bhreṇa̍ vasata̱ parva̍tāsas taviṣī̱yanta̍ḥ śrathayanta vī̱rāḥ ||
5i̱mām ū̱ ṣv ā̍su̱rasya̍ śru̱tasya̍ ma̱hīm mā̱yāṁ varu̍ṇasya̱ pra vo̍cam | māne̍neva tasthi̱vām̐ a̱ntari̍kṣe̱ vi yo ma̱me pṛ̍thi̱vīṁ sūrye̍ṇa ||
6i̱mām ū̱ nu ka̱vita̍masya mā̱yām ma̱hīṁ de̱vasya̱ naki̱r ā da̍dharṣa | eka̱ṁ yad u̱dnā na pṛ̱ṇanty enī̍r āsi̱ñcantī̍r a̱vana̍yaḥ samu̱dram ||
translation.text:
3Varuṇa lets the big cask, opening downward, flow through the heaven and earth and air's midregion. Therewith the universe's Sovran waters earth as the shower of rain bedews the barley.
4When Varuṇa is fain for milk he moistens the sky, the land, and earth to her foundation. Then straight the mountains clothe them in the rain-cloud: the Heroes, putting forth their vigour, loose them.
5I will declare this mighty deed of magic, of glorious Varuṇa the Lord Immortal, Who standing in the firmament hath meted the earth out with the Sun as with a measure.
6None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God's mighty deed of magic, Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.85.7-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 31); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 399v
translation.original_text:
7a̱rya̱mya̍ṁ varuṇa mi̱trya̍ṁ vā̱ sakhā̍yaṁ vā̱ sada̱m id bhrāta̍raṁ vā | ve̱śaṁ vā̱ nitya̍ṁ varu̱ṇāra̍ṇaṁ vā̱ yat sī̱m āga̍ś cakṛ̱mā śi̱śratha̱s tat ||
8ki̱ta̱vāso̱ yad ri̍ri̱pur na dī̱vi yad vā̍ ghā sa̱tyam u̱ta yan na vi̱dma | sarvā̱ tā vi ṣya̍ śithi̱reva̍ de̱vādhā̍ te syāma varuṇa pri̱yāsa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
7If we have sinned against the man who loves us, have ever wronged a brother, friend, or comrade, The neighbour ever with us, or a stranger, O Varuṇa, remove from us the trespass.
8If we, as gamesters cheat at play, have cheated, done wrong unwittingly or sinned of purpose, Cast all these sins away like loosened fetters, and, Varuṇa let us be thine own beloved.
